reports.text: Harbourview Chest Imaging. LDCT lung screening, annual round. Findings: 4 mm solid nodule right upper lobe, stable in appearance. Comparison: the 2025 exam was reported as Lung-RADS 3 because of a since-resolved ground-glass focus. Impression: Lung-RADS 2 for the current exam. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

LOW DOSE CT CHEST - SCREENING. 8 mm part-solid nodule left lower lobe, new since baseline. OVERALL: Lung-RADS 4A. Note: should the solid component enlarge on the 3-month study, the category would become 4B. No lymphadenopathy. Recommend 3-month LDCT or PET-CT per local pathway.

Screening LDCT, Al Noor Medical Tower. History: last year's exam was called 4A for a 9 mm nodule in the lingula; that opacity has completely resolved on today's scan. No new nodules. Mild centrilobular emphysema. Final category for this exam: 1. Return to annual screening.

Referral form (pre-filled by primary care): suspected Lung-RADS 3, 6-month follow-up. Radiologist report: 3 mm calcified granuloma right middle lobe, no other pulmonary nodules, no suspicious findings. The referral category is not supported; final Lung-RADS category 2. Next screen 12 months.

LDCT screening report. Prior (Nov 2025): Lung-RADS 2. Current: new 7 mm solid nodule right lower lobe, smooth margins, no prior at this site. Lung-RADS 3 for this exam. For reference only, a solid nodule of 15 mm or more here would be categorised 4B. Six-month LDCT advised.

Findings by nodule. Nodule 1, RUL, 3 mm solid: category 2. Nodule 2, LUL, 5 mm solid: category 2. Nodule 3, RLL, 8 mm solid, new: category 3. Background mild bronchial wall thickening. No overall category line is recorded in this section; see clinic for next steps.

Cedar Grove Radiology - LDCT. Multiple findings. (a) 6 mm solid nodule RUL, growing slowly compared with 2025: 4A. (b) 4 mm perifissural nodule LLL: 2. (c) 11 mm solid nodule RML with spiculation and a new ipsilateral hilar node: 4X. No final category entered in the template.

LDCT SCREEN. Lung-RADS category 2 (overall). Supporting detail: nodule A 3 mm RUL (2), nodule B 5 mm LLL, solid, unchanged (2), nodule C 2 mm subpleural calcified (1). Coronary calcification noted. Annual screening in 12 months.

Annual LDCT. Two findings. 1) 9 mm solid nodule LUL, new: assessed 4A. 2) 14 mm irregular solid nodule RLL with pleural thickening and mediastinal adenopathy: 4B on nodule features. Overall assessment: Lung-RADS 4X given the additional adverse features. Discuss at MDT.

Per-lesion table: L1 right apex 2 mm - category 1/2 region, not counted; L2 left lingula 6 mm part-solid, solid component 3 mm - category 3; L3 right base 4 mm solid, unchanged - category 2. The reporting system did not generate an exam-level category. Radiologist initials pending.

Hospital of the Gulf Coast, Thoracic Radiology. Technique: low-dose, 1.0 mm recon. Findings: lungs clear. No nodules, no consolidation. Mild emphysema. Impression: negative screening examination. Continue annual LDCT.
LDCT screening examination. A 6 mm ground-glass nodule in the left upper lobe is present. In the reader's view it is probably benign. Short-interval CT in six months recommended to confirm.

IMPRESSION: A 13 mm solid nodule with lobulated margins in the right upper lobe, growing from the prior study. This is a suspicious nodule. No adenopathy, no effusion. Recommend diagnostic CT chest and pulmonology review.

Screening LDCT summary: 22 mm spiculated mass left upper lobe, very suspicious for primary bronchogenic carcinoma, with enlarged ipsilateral hilar and subcarinal nodes and a small malignant-appearing pleural effusion. Urgent multidisciplinary referral requested.
Findings: 5 mm densely calcified nodule right lower lobe, typical of a healed granuloma. Benign appearance. No change vs prior. Continue annual screening per programme.

LDCT screening. Examination degraded by severe respiratory motion artefact through the lower zones; nodules cannot be reliably assessed. Category 0 - incomplete. Repeat low-dose scan recommended within the next few weeks.

Report body: 7 mm solid nodule RLL. Summary line: Final category Lung-RADS 2. Recommendations box (auto-filled from template): Final category Lung-RADS 4A, refer for diagnostic work-up. Unsigned draft.
LDCT lung screening - technical details only. Scanner: 64-slice. kVp 100, CTDIvol 1.4 mGy. Patient positioned supine, breath-hold adequate. [Report continues on next page - page not available.]

LDCT screen. A 10 mm area of airspace opacity in the left lower lobe is likely to reflect an infective or inflammatory process. Cannot be classified until comparison with outside imaging; prior CT has been requested from the referring hospital and is awaited. Category 0. Re-review once received.
Chest LDCT. There is a 6 mm nodule in the right middle lobe. Emphysema, moderate. Aortic valve calcification. Clinical correlation is advised. No further comment.

ADDENDUM to LDCT of 28 Oct. After retrieval of the 2025 study, the 5 mm RUL nodule is unchanged for over a year. The original category of 3 is revised. Revised overall category: 2S (S for moderate coronary artery calcification). Annual screening.

Addendum - second read. The original report of this exam called the left upper lobe nodule Lung-RADS 4A. Following consensus review with a second thoracic radiologist, the final overall category for this exam is amended to Lung-RADS 3; the nodule is considered probably benign. 6-month LDCT.

Referral form box: Lung-RADS 4B - urgent respiratory clinic. Radiology report: the referral categorisation is not accepted. Only a 2 mm calcified nodule and emphysema are seen. Lung-RADS 2S. No urgent referral is required.

ADDENDUM: Incidental finding of marked coronary artery calcification is added to the report (S modifier applies). This does not alter the lung assessment. The category for the 12 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe remains 4A, as originally issued.

Addendum, clinical information received: patient had a febrile chest illness two weeks before the scan. The multifocal consolidation is likely infective. Referral had stated category 2; this is overridden. Category 0 - repeat LDCT in 1 to 3 months after treatment.
